subject: Human Body
title: Glucagon: The Counter Signal
description: A 60-second lesson on Glucagon: The Counter Signal.

hook.text: Skipped lunch? Your blood sugar drops. The pancreas detects this and releases glucagon to raise it back up.

buildup.text: Glucagon tells the liver to convert stored glycogen back into glucose and release it into the bloodstream.

discovery.text: Insulin and glucagon work as opposites. Insulin lowers sugar after meals. Glucagon raises it between meals.

twist.text: In type 2 diabetes, glucagon production is often dysregulated too.

climax.text: Glucagon prevents dangerous blood sugar drops.

punchline.text: Insulin and glucagon are a seesaw. One lowers, one raises.

quiz.question: What does glucagon do?
options: It helps cells absorb glucose from the blood
It tells the liver to release stored glucose into the blood
It converts fat into glucose in muscle cells
